Plus, its lime-spiked nuoc cham dressing brings further zingy flavour to the fore. Yum!

Key ingredients in Brendan Pang’s garlic butter chicken noodles

Dried rice vermicelli noodles: a handy pantry staple for creating speedy dinners, dried rice vermicelli noodles form the base for soaking up all those delicious garlic-butter juices.
Chicken tenderloins: thinly sliced, these cook fast and get the golden caramelised treatment in this recipe. 
Garlic cloves: Brendan uses 4 finely chopped garlic cloves for maximum depth of flavour in this delicious and easy Vietnamese noodle recipe.
Unsalted butter: this puts the ‘butter’ in ‘garlic butter chicken noodles’ 
Soy sauce: light soy sauce bolsters the salty umami richness of this recipe.
Fish sauce: a mainstay in Vietnamese cuisine, fish sauce is a must-add for depth of flavour in this chicken noodle recipe.
White sugar: for balance, Brendan uses white sugar to round out the savoury sauce additions.
Nuoc cham dressing: this flavourful dressing is brought to life with garlic, chilli, white sugar, fish sauce and fresh lime juice (plus hot water). With so few ingredients, you might be surprised by how much bold flavour this dressing brings to the plate.
Toppings: ground black pepper, fresh herbs (think coriander, Thai basil and mint), thinly sliced red chilli, fried shallots and wedges of lime complete the picture (and flavour profile) of this delicious Vietnamese noodles recipe.


Need even more noodle inspiration? Check out these delicious noodle recipes.
Recipe by cookbook author and MasterChef alumnus, Brendan Pang
ingredients: Fresh herb sprigs (Brendan uses coriander, Thai basil and mint), to serve
1 small fresh red chilli, thinly sliced
1 small fresh red chilli, finely chopped
instructions: To make the Nuoc cham dressing, combine garlic, chilli, sugar, fish sauce, lime juice and hot water in a small bowl. Taste and adjust seasoning, as desired. Set aside.
Soak or cook rice noodles following package directions. Drain and rinse under cold running water to prevent sticking. Set aside.

Heat oil in a wok or large frying pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken and stir-fry for 3-4 minutes or until starting to brown around the edges. Reduce heat to medium. Add garlic and butter. Cook, basting the chicken with the garlic butter, for 1-2 minutes. Add soy sauce, fish sauce, sugar and pepper. Stir-fry, tossing to coat the chicken in the glossy fragrant sauce.

Divide the cooked noodles among serving bowls. Drizzle with some nuoc cham dressing. Use a slotted egg lift or spoon to top the noodles with the chicken, reserving the butter mixture. Add fresh herbs to the bowls. Sprinkle with sliced chilli and fried shallots. Drizzle with the reserved garlic butter. Serve with lime wedges. Watch our step-by-step video below to see how to make Brendan Pang's Vietnamese garlic butter chicken noodles.

recipes.title: Boerewors sausage roll recipe
recipes.description: No, this recipe is not cooked on the braai, but it certainly celebrates it, blending two of South Africa’s and Australia’s most iconic recipes – boerewors and a flaky sausage roll!
ingredients: 2 sheets frozen butter puff pastry, halved
3.00 gm nigella or black sesame seeds
instructions: Preheat oven to 220°C/200°C fan-forced. Cook coriander seeds in a dry frying pan over medium heat until toasted and aromatic. Transfer to a mortar and use a pestle to crush.

Heat oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat. Add onion and cook, stirring, for 3-4 minutes or until softened. Add garlic, pepper, nutmeg, allspice and two-thirds of the crushed coriander. Season. Cook for 2 minutes, then remove pan from the heat. Set aside to cool.

Place spice mixture and beef mince in a bowl. Squeeze filling from pork sausages into the bowl. Discard the skins. Add breadcrumbs and egg. Use clean hands to mix together well. Season. Cover and place in the fridge until ready to use.

Thaw the pastry slightly (you want to make sure it is not too soft to handle). Place the pastry sheets on a lightly floured bench (Alternatively, lay down a large piece of baking paper to prevent sticking). Join the short edges together, slightly overlapping. Use a fork to crimp the edges together to seal and make 1 long strip of pastry.

Form a sausage with the mince along the pastry. Brush the pastry edges with extra egg. Roll the pastry over to enclose and seal the edge. Start with 1 end of the sausage roll in the centre then bring around the remaining sausage shape to form a spiral. Leave a 2cm gap within the spiral as the pastry will expand. Transfer to a baking tray. Brush with egg. Sprinkle over nigella or sesame seeds and reserved crushed coriander seeds. Season with salt and pepper. Bake for 40 minutes or until golden and cooked through. You want no raw pastry bits in the middle.

Meanwhile, to make the tomato relish, heat the oil in a saucepan over medium high heat. Add tomatoes and cook for 2-3 minutes until they start to blister. Season. Add garlic and cook for 1 minute or until aromatic. Add sugar, tomato paste, vinegar and basil, if using. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 5-6 minutes. Use a potato masher or back of a spoon to crush the tomatoes in the pan. Season. Remove from the heat and set aside to cool.
Serve with the sausage roll with the tomato relish. Watch our step-by-step video below to see how to make Warren Mendes' Boerewors sausage roll recipe.

recipes.title: Creamy potato salad dressing recipe
recipes.description: This is one potato salad dressing recipe you’ll want to bookmark.
instructions: Place the sour cream, mayonnaise, vinegar and blue cheese in a food processor and process until smooth. Transfer to a bowl.
Stir in chives and dill. Season.

recipes.title: Chicken and black bean burritos recipe
recipes.description:
Chicken burritos are quick and easy to make, packed with so many great flavours and get the thumbs up from the whole family. Both adults and kids will love wrapping their hands around these warm tortillas filled with tender seasoned chicken, rice, colourful veg, grated cheese and deliciously good-for-you black beans. 
Why we love serving these chicken and black bean burritos…
These chicken burritos are packed with balanced ingredients and full of flavour, which is what makes them so family friendly. Pre-prepared Mexican inspired sauce gives the chicken a wonderfully mild and spicy tang and is also used in the creamy sauce, which you can generously drizzle over the open ends of the burritos. Paired with vibrant salad vegies, brown rice and filling black beans, you can always rest easy knowing that when you feed the kids burritos, you’re giving them a meal they will hands-down love that will leave them feeling satisfied, too. 
What’s more, these chicken burritos are just so versatile, which fits in perfectly with our super-busy lifestyles. They’re excellent for a quick lunch, easy mid-week dinner, picnic, or made ahead for a work or school lunch box. You can also customise them to suit – add some halved cherry tomatoes or chopped long red chillies to the filling, switch out the avocado for guacamole, or stir some drained canned corn kernels into the cooked brown rice. 
💡 Tip: Enjoy Mexican inspired Mondays at your place! 
Place all the readied ingredients in bowls on the table and then let the family fill their own burritos, using the ingredients they love the best.
Key ingredients in these burritos

Old El PasoTM Chipotle Tacos Cooking Sauce: this delicious blend of diced tomatoes, onions, paprika, cumin, coriander and chipotle chili powder makes your chicken burritos sing with flavour. It’s also lovely and mild, so will appeal to all. 
Old El PasoTM Mild Black beans: black beans are a Mexican inspired staple and a superfood containing loads of fibre and antioxidants. Dense and meaty, they are a clever way to bulk up this meal to make it feel more substantial. 
Old El PasoTM Jumbo Tortillas: super soft and flexible, these extra large wraps can hold a lot more filling than regular tortillas, making them ideal for the hungriest members of your family. Preparing them is as easy as popping them in the microwave for 35 seconds, but you can heat them in the oven as well.
Barbecued chicken: using shredded barbecued chicken for these burritos conveniently cuts down the cooking and prep times, plus adds extra flavour. You can also use cooked and shredded chicken breast, if that’s what you have on hand. 
Capsicum: these are the ultimate Mexican vegetable, offering a distinct flavour, healthy vitamins, vibrant colours (as we use both red and green capsicums) and a delightful crunch to these chicken burritos.
Microwave brown rice: another convenient addition to these burritos, brown rice is healthy and only takes 90 seconds in the microwave to prepare. You can use cooked regular brown rice instead, if you desire.
Baja sauce: this creamy sauce made by mixing yoghurt, sour cream, coriander leaves, lime juice and a little Mexican inspired sauce all together is quick to make and out-of-this-world delicious. We feel it really enhances these burritos but, if you’re short on time, a dollop of sour cream on the burritos is the next best thing. 

Want to mix up your Mexican inspired Mondays? We have loads more burritos for you to wrap your mouths around, made with chicken, as well as beef mince, lamb and fish, or just vegetables, if that's your preference. And because Mexican never gets old, here is a whole host of Mexican inspired dishes that you can share with your family and friends on any day of the week!
ingredients: 170g pkt Old El Paso™ Chipotle Tacos Cooking Sauce
425g can Old El Paso™ Mild Black Beans, rinsed, drained
instructions: To make Baja sauce, combine all ingredients in a serving bowl. Season. Cover and place in the fridge until required.
Heat oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Add onion and capsicum and cook, stirring, for 5-6 minutes or until charred and just tender. Transfer to a bowl.

Reserve 2 tsp Old El Paso™ Chipotle Tacos Cooking Sauce. Add the chicken and remaining chipotle sauce to the frying pan. Cook over medium heat, stirring occasionally, for 4-5 minutes or until heated through.
Meanwhile, heat rice and Old El Paso™ Jumbo Tortillas following packet directions.

Place tortillas on a flat surface. Top with the rice, chicken mixture, avocado, cheese, capsicum mixture and Old El Paso™ mild Black Beans along the centre. Fold in exposed short ends of the tortilla, then roll up tightly to enclose the filling. Wrap in baking paper and foil to secure the roll. Cut in half.
Swirl reserved chipotle sauce through the baja sauce. Serve the sauce and lime cheeks alongside the burritos.

recipes.title: Overnight chia oats with berries recipe
recipes.description: These overnight oats are made extra creamy thanks to the addition of your favourite nut butter. Just mix and chill before bed, and you'll have a healthy, low calorie breakfast ready to eat as soon as you wake up.
ingredients: 125ml (1/2 cup) unsweetened almond or skim milk
instructions: Combine the oats, chia seeds, pepitas, peanut butter, cinnamon, milk and honey in a jar or container. Cover. Place in the fridge overnight to soak.
Top the oat mixture with yoghurt and berries to serve.

recipes.title: Savoury French toast
recipes.description: A more nutritious version of popular breakfast item French toast. This recipe, created by our expert nutritionist, is designed to give you all the wholegrains, good fats and protein you need to start your day right. It's also perfect for those who don't enjoy sweet brekkies.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C/160°C fan forced. Line a baking tray with baking paper. Place tomatoes on the prepared tray and roast for 10 minutes or until slightly wilted.
Whisk together the eggs and milk in a large shallow bowl.

Lightly spray a large non-stick frying pan with oil and heat over medium heat. Dip bread slices, 1 at a time, in egg mixture until well soaked. Cook for 2 minutes each side or until golden brown and egg is set. Repeat with remaining bread and egg mixture.
Serve French toast topped with tomatoes, avocado and basil.

recipes.title: Baked berry oats recipe
recipes.description: Start the day with a protein hit from these baked berry oats. This healthy brekky will fill you up and keep you going 'till lunchtime!
ingredients: 150g (1 cup) frozen mixed berries, plus extra, to serve
instructions: Preheat oven to 190C/170C fan forced. Lightly grease four 250ml (1 cup) ovenproof ramekins or dishes with olive oil.

Combine the oats, hemp seeds, baking powder and cinnamon in a large bowl. Place the banana, eggs and milk in a separate bowl. Mix until well combined. Add the banana mixture to the oat mixture and stir until just combined (do not overmix).

Divide half the oat mixture among prepared ramekins. Top with half the berries. Top with the remaining oat mixture then remaining berries. Place ramekins on a baking tray. Bake for 20 minutes or until golden, puffed and set. Serve warm with yoghurt and extra berries.

recipes.title: Choc-banana chia pudding recipe
recipes.description: Want a healthy breakfast that tastes like an indulgent dessert? This make-ahead choc-banana chia pudding has made our brekky dreams come true.
instructions: Peel 1 banana half. Place in a bowl with cocoa. Use a fork to mash. Stir through milk. Add chia. Stir until combined. Cover and place in the fridge overnight to thicken.
Peel and thinly slice remaining banana. Spoon chia pudding into a serving glass. Top with banana and peanut butter.

recipes.title: Healthy granola recipe
recipes.description: Store-bought granola products tend to be loaded with sugar and additives so to ensure your breakfast is as nutritious and healthy as possible, you can always mix your own! It's super easy and if you make a big batch, it will store for a number of weeks so it's ready to go in the morning when you are. Our mix includes lots of nuts and seeds, making it super crunchy and just perfect with some natural yoghurt.
instructions: Preheat oven to 160C/140C fan forced. Line 2 large baking trays with baking paper.

Combine oats, buckwheat, macadamias, pecans, oat bran, pepitas and sunflower seeds in a large bowl. Combine the maple syrup, vanilla and cinnamon in a small bowl. Add the maple syrup mixture to the oat mixture and stir until well combined.

Divide mixture between prepared trays. Spread to cover base. Bake, stirring 2-3 times during cooking, for 20-30 minutes or until golden and crisp. Divide cranberries between trays. Stir until combined. Set aside to cool completely. Store granola in an airtight jar for up to three weeks (see note).

recipes.title: Protein-packed breakfast bowl recipe
recipes.description: Ready in 10 minutes, this breakfast bowl, packed with quinoa, avocado and egg, will get your day off to a healthy start.
instructions: Place the spinach in a colander. Pour over boiling water. Use clean hands to squeeze any excess liquid from the spinach.
Arrange quinoa, spinach, egg and avocado in a serving bowl. Drizzle over lemon juice and olive oil. Top with almonds to serve.

recipes.title: Mango and passionfruit swirl smoothie bowl recipe
recipes.description: Enjoy a healthy brekky with this delicious mango smoothie bowl. You only need 5 minutes to whip it up.
instructions: Place the mango, banana, almond milk, yoghurt and chia in a blender and blend until thick and creamy. Transfer to a serving bowl.
Serve topped with passionfruit and extra chia.

recipes.title: Poached pear bircher muesli recipe
recipes.description: Create this impressive cafe-style brekkie at home. A easy, healthy way to start the weekend.
instructions: Combine the oats, grated pear, ground cinnamon, 1 cup (250ml) apple juice, half the yoghurt and half the vanilla in a large bowl. Cover and place in the fridge for 4 hours or overnight to soak.

Meanwhile, place whole pears, cinnamon stick or quill, star anise, saffron, if using, remaining apple juice and remaining vanilla in a saucepan. Add enough water to cover the pears. Cover with a disc of baking paper. Bring to the boil over high heat. Reduce heat to low. Cook for 40-45 mins or until the pears are very tender.

Use a slotted spoon to transfer the pears to a heatproof bowl. Bring the syrup in the pan to the boil over high heat. Cook for 10 mins or until the syrup reduces by half and thickens. Pour over the pears in the bowl. Place in the fridge to chill.
Spoon the muesli mixture into serving bowls. Top with poached pears, remaining yoghurt and hazelnut. Drizzle with syrup.

recipes.title: The new avo toast recipe
recipes.description: Upgrade the smashed avocado toast breakfast staple with beetroot hommus and goat's cheese.
ingredients: 1/2 large ripe avocado, stoned, thickly sliced
instructions: Toast the sourdough. Place on serving plates.
Place the avocado in a bowl and use a fork to gently mash. Spread onto the toast. Season. Top with the hommus and goat’s cheese. Sprinkle with the chive and rocket.

recipes.title: Low-cal cinnamon ginger granola recipe
recipes.description: This healthier granola has only natural sweeteners but these golden clusters still have all the crunch you desire. A go-to quick breakfast option, just add your favourite yoghurt or milk.
ingredients: 200g (1 cup) mixed chopped nuts (cashews, almonds, walnuts, brazil nuts)
2-3 tsp finely grated fresh ginger, to taste
instructions: Preheat oven to 180C/160C fan forced. Line 2 baking trays with non-stick baking paper.

Place the coconut oil, 1 tbs honey, puffed quinoa, mixed nuts, rolled oats, coconut, pepitas, chia and hemp seeds, ginger, vanilla seeds, cinnamon, cardamom and cloves in a large bowl. Stir until well coated.
Divide mixture among prepared trays, spreading out evenly. Bake for 10 minutes. Stir with a spatula. Bake for a further 5-10 minutes or until light golden and crisp.
Drizzle with the remaining honey. Mix well. Set aside on trays to cool completely. Serve with kefir and blueberries, if using.

recipes.title: Chai-spiced overnight oats recipe
recipes.description: Soaked in chai-infused milk, this healthier overnight oats breakfast bowl is the perfect way to start your day.
instructions: Place the milk into a small saucepan and add the teabags over medium heat and bring just to simmer. Turn off heat and set aside for 15 minutes, to infuse. Stir in 2 tablespoons of the maple syrup.
Combine the oats and chia seeds in a bowl or airtight container. Pour in the chai mixture (discard teabags) and stir well. Cover and store in the fridge overnight.
Divide oat mixture among serving bowls. Top with yoghurt, mango, raspberries and pistachios. Drizzle with the remaining maple syrup.

recipes.title: Granola crumb recipe
recipes.description: Add a crunchy, nutritious topping to your morning yoghurt and fruit with this low-calorie granola dust.
instructions: Preheat oven to 170C/150C fan-forced. Line a large baking tray with baking paper.

Combine the oats, almonds, coconut, pepitas, sunflower seeds, maple syrup and cinnamon in a large bowl and stir well to coat. Spread mixture evenly over prepared tray. Bake for 25-30 minutes, stirring every 10 minutes, until golden and crunchy. Stir through goji berries and rind. Set aside to cool completely.
Add half the granola to a food processor and process until a coarse crumb forms. Repeat with the remaining granola. Transfer to an airtight jar or container (see note).

recipes.title: Peanut butter and raspberry overnight oats
recipes.description: For extra fruity goodness, stir a handful of blueberries into the oat mixture before soaking overnight – they’ll create pops of juicy flavour.
instructions: Combine the oats, chia seeds, banana, oat milk and peanut butter in a medium bowl. Cover with plastic wrap. Place in the fridge overnight to soak.

Meanwhile, place raspberries and sugar in a saucepan over low heat. Cook, stirring, for 5 mins or until sugar dissolves and raspberries soften. Transfer to a blender. Blend until smooth. Set aside to cool completely.
3. Layer the raspberry puree and oat mixture in serving jars or bowls. Decorate with the extra raspberries, extra peanut butter, almond, pistachio, pepitas, extra chia seeds and sesame seeds.

recipes.title: Potato rosti with poached egg
recipes.description: Serve this moreish golden potato rosti with a perfectly poached egg, salmon and avocado for a yummy brunch everyone will love.
ingredients: 6 large brushed potatoes, peeled, coarsely grated
20.00 ml drained baby capers, coarsely chopped
instructions: Preheat oven to 100°C. Line a baking tray with baking paper. Combine the potato and onion in a large bowl. Transfer to a colander. Use your hands to squeeze as much liquid from the potato mixture as possible. Transfer the potato mixture to a medium bowl. Stir in the butter. Season well.

Add enough oil to a large non-stick frying pan to cover the base. Place over medium heat. Spoon two 1/2-cup portions of mixture into the pan. Use a spatula to flatten each portion to a 10cm disc. Cook for 3-4 mins each side or until golden brown and cooked through. Transfer to a heatproof plate lined with paper towel. Place in oven to keep warm. Repeat in 3 more batches with the remaining potato mixture.

Meanwhile, bring a saucepan of water to a simmer over high heat. Add vinegar. Crack 1 egg into a small bowl. Stir the water to create a whirlpool. Pour the egg into the centre of whirlpool. Cook, without stirring, for 3 mins for a runny yolk or until cooked to your liking. Use a slotted spoon to transfer to a bowl. Repeat with remaining eggs.
To make chive & dill dressing, whisk oil, vinegar, mustard, chives, dill and caper in a bowl until combined. Season.
Divide rosti, salmon, avocado, rocket and poached eggs among serving plates. Drizzle with dressing.

recipes.title: Better-for-you banana pancakes
recipes.description: These healthier high-protein pancakes prove that breakfasts don't have to be loaded with sugar to be sweet.
ingredients: 150g (1 cup) wholemeal plain flour or purple wheat plain flour (see tip)
60g (1/2 cup) almond meal or hazelnut meal
18.40 gm virgin macadamia oil or coconut oil
instructions: Place the banana, flour, nut meal, cinnamon, eggs, kefir and 2 tsp oil in a blender or a food processor. Blend or process until smooth and well combined. Add the baking powder and process for a further 5-10 seconds, until just combined.

Heat a non-stick frying pan over medium-high heat. Add 1 tsp of the remaining oil. Pour 1/4-cupful of batter into the pan and gently swirl to create a pancake about 12cm in diameter. Cook for 1-2 minutes, until bubbles begin to form on the surface and the pancake is golden underneath. Carefully flip and cook for a further 1-2 minutes, until golden on both sides and cooked through. Transfer to a plate and cover loosely with foil to keep warm. Repeat with the remaining mixture (and remaining 1 tsp oil, if needed) until all the batter has been used.
Divide the pancakes among serving plates. Top each stack with 11 ⁄2 tbs ricotta, if you like. Scatter with the mixed berries and serve with a light drizzle of maple syrup.

recipes.title: Breakfast quinoa and red fruit salad
recipes.description: Shake up your morning routine with our easy breakfast fruit salad.
ingredients: 500g piece watermelon, peeled, very thinly sliced
40.00 ml finely shredded fresh mint leaves
instructions: Cook quinoa in a medium saucepan following packet directions. Drain. Refresh under cold water. Drain (see notes).
Combine passionfruit pulp and lime juice in a jug. Arrange fruit on a serving platter. Top with quinoa. Drizzle passionfruit mixture over salad. Sprinkle with mint. Serve.

recipes.title: Banana-berry breakfast biscuits
recipes.description: Kick off your day with these sweet and crunchy breakfast biscuits. They store well, so make a big batch to keep in the freezer.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C/160°C fan-forced. Line 2 baking trays with baking paper.

Reserve 1 tablespoon each of the oats and almonds. Place remaining oats and almonds, banana, almond spread, oil, maple syrup, vanilla and mixed spice in a large bowl. Stir until combined. Stir in blackberries.

Place 1/4 cup of mixture, 4cm apart, on prepared trays. Sprinkle with reserved oats and almonds. Bake for 25 minutes or until golden and firm. Stand for 10 minutes. Transfer to a wire rack to cool. Serve (see notes).

recipes.title: The new green smoothie
recipes.description: Create a nourishing green smoothie with this healthy avocado, apple, cucumber, zucchini and spinach recipe.
ingredients: 1 ripe avocado, stoned, peeled, coarsely chopped
1 Granny Smith apple, cored, coarsely chopped
instructions: Place the avocado, spinach, cucumber, apple, coconut water, ginger, lime and ice in a blender and blend until smooth.
Pour the avocado mixture evenly among serving glasses. Sprinkle evenly with the lime zest, pepitas and chia seeds. Serve immediately.

recipes.title: Avocado quinoa brekkie bowl
recipes.description: Bulk out your bowl with any veggies you can find in the fridge including chopped carrot, zucchini or shredded spinach.
ingredients: 2 corn cobs, husks and silks removed
instructions: Heat 1 teaspoon of the oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add paprika, cumin and ground coriander. Cook, stirring, for 30 seconds or until aromatic. Add the quinoa and 2 cups (500ml) water. Bring to the boil. Reduce heat to low. Cook, covered, for 15 mins or until quinoa is tender and liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat. Set aside, covered, for 10 mins to stand. Use a fork to separate grains.

Meanwhile, heat a barbecue grill or chargrill on high. Cook corn, turning, for 8-10 mins or until lightly charred and tender. Use a small serrated knife to run down the side of cob to release kernels. Add to quinoa mixture with tomato.
Place half the spring onion, half the coriander leaves and half the mint in a food processor with the lemon juice and remaining oil. Process until finely chopped. Season.

Fill a deep saucepan two-thirds full with water. Bring to the boil over high heat. Crack 1 egg into a small cup. Use a large spoon to stir the water to create a whirlpool. Carefully pour the egg into the centre of the whirlpool. Cook, without stirring, for 2 mins for a soft yolk. Use a slotted spoon to transfer to a plate. Repeat with the remaining eggs.
Divide quinoa mixture, avocado and eggs among serving bowls. Sprinkle with lemon zest and the remaining spring onion, coriander leaves and mint. Drizzle with the coriander pesto.

recipes.title: Breakfast hash waffles
recipes.description: For the ultimate breakfast, try our two-ingredient crispy hash brown waffles, topped with avocado, egg and tomatoes.
ingredients: 40.00 ml chopped fresh chives, plus extra, to serve
Mixed cherry tomatoes, halved, to serve
instructions: Place the potato in a saucepan and cover with cold water. Place over medium heat. Cover and bring to the boil. Uncover and boil for 5 minutes or until the potato is partially cooked (it should be cooked on the outside, but starchy and sticky on the inside). Transfer the potato to a plate and set aside until cool enough to handle.
Coarsely grate the potato into a large bowl. Add the chives and season. Use your hands to mix until well combined.

Preheat oven to 100C/80C fan forced. Spray the top and bottom of a non-stick waffle maker generously with oil. Place 1 cup of the potato mixture onto the base and use damp fingertips to spread out evenly. Close the lid and turn on heat. Cook for 7 minutes or until golden. Turn off the waffle maker and gently transfer to a plate. Keep warm in the oven. Repeat with the remaining potato mixture to make 3 more waffles.

Meanwhile, heat a non-stick frying pan over medium heat. Add the chorizo and cook, turning halfway, for 4 minutes or until golden. Transfer to a plate. Crack the eggs into the pan and cook for 3 minutes for sunny-side up or until cooked to your liking.
Divide the potato waffles among serving plates. Top with avocado, eggs, chorizo, tomato and mixed salad leaves. Drizzle with sauce and serve sprinkled with extra chives.

recipes.title: Beetroot and apple porridge
recipes.description: Serve up a delicious breakfast bowl with this one-pan beetroot and apple porridge topped with fresh blueberries, pepitas and maple syrup.
ingredients: 515.00 gm milk, plus extra to serve
84.38 gm maple syrup, plus extra to serve (optional)
instructions: Place beetroot, milk and 1 cup water in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 5 to 7 minutes or until beetroot is tender.
Meanwhile, coarsely grate 1 apple.
Stir oats, salt, mixed spice and maple syrup into beetroot mixture. Cook over medium-low heat for 5 minutes or until oats have softened and thickened. Stir in grated apple.

Core remaining apple and cut in half. Cut into thin slices. Divide porridge among serving bowls. Top with apple, pepitas and blueberries. Drizzle with extra maple syrup, if using. Serve with extra milk.

recipes.title: Overnight chia porridge
recipes.description: Super charge your oats while you sleep for the perfect healthy breakfast.
instructions: Combine the oats, chia seeds, cinnamon and almond milk in a bowl. Cover and place in the fridge overnight to soak.
Transfer the oat mixture to a saucepan. Cook, stirring, over medium-low heat for 5-10 minutes or until thick and creamy.
Divide the porridge among bowls. Swirl some jam through some yoghurt. Dollop over the porridge. Top with raspberries and almonds and drizzle with maple syrup.

recipes.title: Glazed cinnamon roll scones recipe
recipes.description: This delicious, warming morning tea recipe sees cinnamon rolls and scones combine in my glazed cinnamon roll scones recipe.
instructions: Preheat oven to 220°C/200°C fan forced. Line a baking tray with baking paper. Place butter, brown sugar and cinnamon in a bowl and stir until mixture is a thick paste. Set aside.

Place flour and cream in a bowl and stir until just combined. Turn out onto a lightly floured surface and knead briefly until smooth (do not over-knead). Use a rolling pin to roll out dough to form a 25cm x 45cm rectangle. Top the dough with the cinnamon mixture and evenly spread all over. With 1 long side facing you, use a sharp knife or pastry cutter to slice dough vertically into 3.5cm-wide strips. One at a time, roll up each strip of dough and arrange together, just touching, on the prepared tray. Brush tops with a little extra thickened cream. Bake for 15 minutes or until golden.
Meanwhile, place icing sugar and extra thickened cream in a small bowl and stir until smooth.
Spread icing over warm rolls. Serve warm or at room temperature.

recipes.title: Creamy rice cooker porridge recipe
recipes.description: We just learnt the rice cooker presents the perfect method for making easy, creamy porridge.
instructions: Place oats, water, milk and vanilla in a rice cooker. Stir to combine. Cover with the lid and cook on the ‘congee/porridge’ setting for 1 hour or until the oats are soft. Stir well to combine.
Divide oat mixture among serving bowls. Drizzle with milk and top with banana. Drizzle with maple syrup and sprinkle with cinnamon, to serve.

recipes.title: 2-ingredient protein booster recipe (no protein powder needed)
recipes.description: My 2-ingredient protein booster recipe adds 10g of protein to your breakfast, which means there’s no need to buy expensive supplements!
ingredients: 200g (1 1/2 cups) Red Tractor Flax, Hemp & Chia Meal
instructions: In batches, place pumpkin seeds in a small food processor and pulse until it resembles a fine meal (don’t overprocess). Transfer to a bowl. Add FHC meal and mix well. Transfer to an airtight container or glass jar. (See notes for storage tips.)

recipes.title: Easy slow cooker poached eggs recipe
recipes.description: We’ve found an easy way to create perfect poached eggs at home: in your slow cooker! Set, forget, and have zero regrets.
instructions: Fill the base of a slow cooker with hot water until 2cm deep. Cover and cook on High for 30 minutes until boiling hot.

Spray four 125ml (1/2 cup) ramekins with oil. Crack 1 egg into each ramekin, then pour 1 tbsp boiling water inside each. Place ramekins in the slow cooker. Cover with the lid and cook on High for 20-25 minutes for jammy yolks and just-set whites.

Use tongs or a tea towel to carefully remove the ramekins from the slow cooker. Set aside for 2 minutes to finish setting the egg whites, while not overcooking the yolks. Hold each ramekin with the tea towel to drain away any watery liquid. Use a spoon to loosen the edge of the eggs and then scoop onto buttered toast. Season, to serve.

recipes.title: Slow cooker ‘boiled’ eggs recipe (the easy way to cook lots of eggs)
recipes.description: If you’re seeking an easy way to cook lots of eggs at once, this slow cooker boiled egg hack is the answer you’ve been looking for.
ingredients: Extra virgin olive oil, to drizzle
instructions: Place eggs in a slow cooker. Cover with cold water. Cover and cook on High for 2 hours 30 minutes to 2 hours 45 minutes. Use a slotted spoon to transfer eggs to an ice bath to stop the cooking process, then set aside for 15 minutes to completely cool.
Peel eggs and slice crossways. Spread sourdough with mashed avocado. Top with the egg slices, season, then drizzle with oil. Serve with rocket.

recipes.title: Emperor's mess recipe (Austrian shredded pancakes)
recipes.description:
These shredded pancakes are a popular dish from Austria, but this, or versions of it, are especially popular in Germany, Hungary and northern Italy. The literal translation of the dish is called emperor’s mess, because apparently the Austrian emperor loved it. 
What exactly is an ‘emperor’s mess’ or Austrian shredded pancakes?

It’s technically a dessert, but it is also perfectly acceptable in Austria and Germany to have this sweet dish for lunch or brunch, especially after a long day of hiking or skiing – it’s a must-try. 
It starts with an eggy pancake that gets torn into bite-sized pieces. If you struggle with flipping and making beautifully rounded pancakes, this recipe is great for you because it’s almost the intention to mess it up! Also, you get more beautifully, slightly crispy, caramelised browned edges this way.
 💡 Tip: Handle the batter with care
Be gentle when folding through the egg whites so that you keep the batter aerated. 
Traditionally, these pancakes are studded with rum-soaked sultanas, but these are completely optional. Serve hot, dusted with icing sugar and topped with warm fruit, especially plum or berry compote.


My dad would make this for me when I was a kid because I have a big sweet tooth and this is probably one of the few sweet dishes you can get away with serving for lunch or dinner. Similar to how Australia has its pancake shaker mixes, you can buy a dry packet mix for these shredded pancakes (also known as kaiserschmarrn) in supermarkets in Germany, so you can whip up the batter in seconds by adding milk, which made it perfect for my busy parents. You can’t get the packet stuff here – but, don’t worry, it tastes even better made from scratch.
Austria versus Australia: how does the Austrian shredded pancake recipe differ from a classic pancake eaten in Australia?
Unlike the classic Australian pancake, in the Austrian variety there is no baking powder or other rising agent used. Instead, the rise and fluffiness comes just from the whipped egg whites folded through the batter.
Also, because Austrian pancakes have more eggs than Aussie pancakes, the taste is richer and almost pudding- or souffle-like – so, don’t worry if your batter is thinner compared to when you’re making regular pancakes. This is what we want.
The batter in this recipe is actually not sweetened that much. The key is to caramelise the shredded pancake pieces in the pan with sugar at the end which provides sweetness, plus you are serving it with dusted icing sugar and a sweet compote.
What do you serve with an emperor’s mess recipe?
Emperor’s mess is traditionally served with plum compote or other fruit compotes, if plums aren’t in season. I specifically like cherries or any other type of red berry compote. In Germany, these are readily available in supermarkets – but because there isn’t an exact  equivalent widely available here, I have included a very simple cherry compote recipe.
It is best served fresh, so I wouldn’t recommend making it ahead.
Key ingredients in this Emperor's mess recipe (Austrian shredded pancakes)

Egg whites: these provide the lift in these pancakes. Whip until soft peaks for fluffiness – don’t take them to stiff peaks overwise they won’t mix well with the batter and they could split. You don’t want any white lumpy bits, just sort of a foamy, liquid batter. 
Egg yolks: these give the pancakes a rich, almost pudding-like texture and taste. You’ll notice that this recipe uses a higher egg-to-flour ratio than you would usually find in a regular pancake recipe. 
Sultanas: these add pops of sweetness. If you hate sultanas, skip them entirely, but if you only ‘just don’t like them’, I encourage you to try them in this dessert. 
Gold rum: this rum suits baking, as a darker one would be too complex. You can swap the rum for water or fruit juice, if you want to keep this recipe alcohol-free.
Plain flour: you’ll be surprised at just how fluffy and cushiony these shredded pancakes are without any added raising agents, so don’t be tempted to use self-raising flour as the pancakes will puff up too much. 
Butter: frying the pancake in butter is essential here, as it contributes to the taste and also helps the carmelisation of the sugar at the end. Swapping for another fat for cooking will impact the flavour. 


If you love European desserts, try these German treats next.
Recipe, images and recipe notes by Recipes and Video Content Creator, Stella Morelli
instructions: Place sultanas and rum in a bowl. Set aside for at least 15 minutes to soak.

Meanwhile, use a sieve to drain cherries into a bowl to save the syrup. Combine cornflour and water in a small bowl until smooth, then stir into the syrup. Transfer to a small saucepan and cook, stirring, over medium-high heat for 1 minute or until thickened. Add cherries to the pan and cook for 1 minute or until heated through. Set aside and keep warm.

Use electric beaters (or a stand mixer) fitted with a whisk attachment to whisk egg yolks, flour, vanilla and half of the milk in a large bowl until smooth. Add remaining milk and whisk until well combined.

Place egg whites and salt in a clean, dry bowl. Use clean electric beaters (or a stand mixer) fitted with a whisk attachment to whisk until foamy. Gradually add caster sugar and whisk until soft peaks form.
In 3 batches, use a spatula to gently fold the egg white mixture into the egg yolk mixture until just combined and no egg white lumps remain in the batter.

Drain sultanas. Heat half of the butter in a large, non-stick frying pan over medium-high heat. Pour in the batter and cook for about 1 minute. Evenly sprinkle sultanas over the top. Reduce heat to low and cook for 5-7 minutes or until the batter is at half set and the base is golden (use an egg lifter to lift and check the colour underneath).

Use the edge of the egg lifter to cut the pancake into quarters (the mixture on top will still be uncooked and foamy). Flip each quarter over. Add remaining butter to the middle of the pan. Cook for 3-4 minutes until golden brown underneath. Use the egg lift to roughly cut the pancake into bite-sized pieces and sprinkle with extra caster sugar. Increase heat to medium-high heat and cook, tossing occasionally, for 1-2 minutes or until the sugar is caramelised. Serve warm, dusted with icing sugar and topped with cherry compote.

recipes.title: Dubai chocolate-style overnight Weet-Bix recipe
recipes.description: Discover a delicious Dubai-style overnight Weet-Bix recipe that’s perfect for breakfast and start your day with a tasty and nutritious twist.
instructions: Coarsely chop 1/4 cup of the Weet-Bix Bites and set aside until required.

Divide the remaining Weet-Bix Bites among four 500ml (2 cup) containers, spreading evenly. Pour 60ml (1/4 cup) water into each container, to wet the cereal. Combine yoghurt and pistachio spread in a bowl. Divide the yoghurt mixture among the containers and spread evenly to cover the Weet-Bix layer.

Place chocolate and coconut oil in a small microwave-safe bowl. Cook on Medium (50%) , stirring every 30 seconds, until melted and smooth. Spoon over the yoghurt mixture in each container and spread to cover. Sprinkle with the reserved chopped Weet-Bix Bites and chopped pistachio. Cover containers with lids or plastic wrap to seal. Place in the fridge overnight, or until set, before serving.

recipes.title: Apple and cinnamon overnight oats recipe (tastes like your fave apple cake!)
recipes.description: Meet the grab-and-go, make-ahead breakfast that’s as easy as it is delicious.
instructions: To make the stewed cinnamon apples, place apple, cinnamon, honey, lemon juice and water in a saucepan over medium heat. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 1-2 minutes or until well combined. Reduce the heat to low and cover. Simmer, stirring occasionally, for 7-8 minutes or until the apple is tender. Set aside to cool slightly.
Meanwhile, place oats, chia seeds, coconut, milk and pepitas in a large bowl and stir to combine.

Place 1/4 cup stewed apple in the bottom of each of 4 x 260ml jars. Divide oat mixture and then remaining stewed apple among the jars. Cover and place in the fridge overnight. To serve, drizzle with extra honey and sprinkle with extra cinnamon and extra pepitas.

recipes.title: Air fryer custard-stuffed crumpets recipe
recipes.description: Creating a sweet and speedy brekky is possible! Better yet, it starts with the humble crumpet.
instructions: Pour 2 tbsp vanilla custard onto the top of each crumpet. Use a knife to spread and slowly press the custard into the crumpet holes.
Place 2 stuffed crumpets in the air fryer basket. Cook at 180C for 10 minutes or until the crumpets are golden. Repeat with the remaining crumpets and custard.

Cut the crumpets in half, diagonally, then stack on a serving plate. Drizzle with golden syrup, to serve. Watch our step-by-step video below to see how to make our air fryer custard-stuffed crumpets recipe.

recipes.title: Air fryer fried eggs recipe
recipes.description:
These air fryer fried eggs are a breakfast dish worth springing out of bed to eat. Easy, hands-free cooking at its best! 
What I love about this air fryer fried eggs recipe
Who doesn’t love eggs for breakfast? Yet sometimes the mess and splatter of a cooked breakfast can seem too much effort, especially if you’re running out the door to work (like I am most days!). 
Recently, I discovered the air fryer can really help on busy mornings. Cooking fried eggs in the air fryer removes any mess on the cooktop and, best of all, you can simply pop your eggs on, put your toast in the toaster and they’re both ready in almost the same amount of time. This hands-free cooking leaves you free to make a cuppa and get ready for work. 

How to get the timing right when frying eggs in the air fryer
After the first 3 minutes, the urge to open the door and check the eggs will be hard to resist – trust me, I know. And yet, it’s important not to open the door and let the residual heat finish the cooking process. We tried cooking the eggs for a minute longer but they firm up quickly – so if you are after the perfect soft-centred fried eggs, it’s better to let the residual heat do the final cooking. However, if you prefer hard-centred eggs, cook them for a further minute and you will be equally surprised at how easy they were to make. 
Which type of ovenproof dish is best for cooking eggs in the air fryer?
For air fryer cooking, it is a good idea to get yourself a few ovenproof dishes that can fit inside the basket of your air fryer. Our air fryer pans, which are available at Coles supermarkets, are the perfect pans to cook eggs in. Interestingly, during testing, we found the darker-coloured pan made a difference in cooking time when compared to the lighter, silver cake pan. The lighter pan took longer to cook the egg whites, which made it easier for the centres to overcook, while the darker pan, which absorbed more heat, cooked more quickly and created a better result for our fried eggs.
 💡 Tip: don’t hold back on the oil
A good amount of oil in the bottom of the pan is essential for that fried egg feel. (We tried cooking with less oil and with an oil spray, but the eggs stuck to the pan and you miss out on the classic crispy fried edge on the egg.) 
See more helpful tips in the recipe notes under this recipe!
To preheat or not to preheat? We have the answer
While testing this recipe, we also tried it with and without preheating the pan and tested cold oil versus hot oil. Having the oil preheated with the basket gives you the best outcome because the eggs start to cook as soon as they hit the hot oil, crisping up the edges and giving you that classic fried eggs texture. 
Which air fryer do we recommend for cooking eggs?
We used the Philips Airfryer with window for this recipe, and we couldn't recommend it more. It's the perfect size for frying eggs, and the nifty window lets you see how your eggs are coming along, helping you to cook them to perfection.
What goes into air fryer fried eggs? Our key ingredients:
Olive oil: eggs cooked in olive oil have an extra delicious flavour, which comes from the hot oil. The best part: if you’re going to do more than one batch, you can reuse the oil in the pan from the previous batch and just top up slightly as needed. 
Eggs: these are undoubtedly the star of this dish. For reference, we use 59g eggs when testing our recipes. 

We love the versatility of the air fryer. If you like the idea of hands-free breakfast cooking, try these 22 air fryer breakfast recipes next.
Recipe, images and notes by Food Director Michelle Southan
instructions: Place an ovenproof pan into an air fryer basket. Pour in olive oil. Preheat at 180C for 2 minutes.
Carefully open the basket and crack the eggs into the hot oil. Close the basket and cook for 3 minutes. Leave the basket closed for a further 1 minute for the heat to finish the cooking process.
Serve the eggs on buttered toast with baby rocket leaves alongside. Watch our step-by-step video below to see how to make our air fryer fried eggs.

recipes.title: Chicken tenders with crunchy coconut crumb
recipes.description: These quick and easy coconut-crumbed chicken strips are perfect served with our speedy three-ingredient sweet and sour dipping sauce.
ingredients: Small fresh coriander leaves, to serve
1-2 tsp white wine vinegar, to taste
instructions: Preheat oven to 200C/180C fan forced. Line a large baking tray with baking paper. Cut the tenderloins in half lengthways, then cut each piece in half crossways.
Place the flour, egg and panko in separate shallow bowls. Add the coconut to the panko and stir to combine.

Toss the chicken in flour and shake off excess. Dip in egg, then roll in the panko mixture, pressing firmly to coat. Transfer to the prepared tray and spray with oil. Bake, turning halfway, for 15 minutes or until golden brown and cooked through.

Meanwhile, to make the dipping sauce, process the pineapple and tomato sauce in a small food processor until almost smooth. Transfer to a small saucepan. Stir in vinegar, to taste. Cook, stirring, over medium-heat heat for 2 minutes or until warm.
Sprinkle the chicken with coriander and serve with the sauce.

recipes.title: Apricot chicken tray bake recipe
recipes.description: A makeover of a classic, this family favourite apricot chicken is now an easy traybake. This super speedy recipe is ready in under one hour.
ingredients: 1 red onion, cut into thin wedges
instructions: Preheat oven to 200C/180C fan-forced. Grease a large baking tray with sides. Line tray with baking paper.

Drain apricots, reserving 1/3 cup juice. Remove leaves from 1 rosemary sprig. Finely chop. Place soup mix, chopped rosemary, oil and reserved juice in a jug. Stir until well combined. Arrange chicken, apricots, potato and onion, in a single layer, on prepared tray. Drizzle over soup mixture. Season with salt and pepper.
Bake, turning chicken and adding remaining rosemary sprigs halfway, for 45 minutes or until chicken is cooked through and potato is tender. Serve.

recipes.title: Doritos-crumbed chicken tenders
recipes.description: How did we make these easy crumbed tenderloins the crispest ever? Coated them in Nacho Cheese Doritos, that's how!
ingredients: 500g Free Range Chicken Tenderloins, halved crossways
170g packet Nacho Cheese Doritos, coarsely chopped
instructions: Place the chicken in a glass or ceramic bowl. Cover with the buttermilk. Cover and place in the fridge for 4 hours or overnight to marinate.
Preheat the oven to 180C/160C fan forced. Line a baking tray with baking paper.
Pulse the corn chips in a food processor until coarsely chopped. Transfer to a plate. Place the egg in a shallow bowl. Place the flour on a separate plate.

Drain the chicken and discard the buttermilk. Place the chicken in the flour, shaking to remove excess. Dip in the egg and then press into the corn chips, pressing well to coat. Transfer to the prepared tray. Spray with oil. Bake for 12-14 minutes or until golden. Serve with salsa.

recipes.title: Butter chicken salad recipe
recipes.description: This 5-ingredient Indian-inspired salad makes for an easy dinner during busy times, or a great last-minute platter for entertaining.
instructions: Preheat a chargrill pan or barbecue grill to medium-high. Combine the chicken fillets and 2 tbs butter chicken sauce in a bowl until well coated. Cook the chicken on the grill for 3-4 minutes each side or until cooked through. Set aside to rest.
Divide the lentils, lettuce and tomatoes among serving plates. Slice the chicken and place on top. Drizzle with remaining warmed butter chicken sauce (see note).

recipes.title: Jerk chicken salad
recipes.description: Ready in 35 minutes, this flavour-packed chicken, pineapple and rice salad is perfect for easy entertaining or as a weeknight dinner.
ingredients: 2 x 250g packets microwave brown rice and quinoa
Thinly sliced red chilli, to serve
instructions: Combine the mixed spice, thyme, cayenne and oil in a shallow glass or ceramic dish. Add the chicken and turn to coat. Set aside until required.
For the dressing, combine all the ingredients in a small jug.

Preheat a chargrill pan over high heat. Add the pineapple and cook, in batches, for 2 minutes each side or until charred. Transfer to a plate. Cook the chicken, in batches, for 2 minutes each side or until cooked through. Transfer to a plate.
Meanwhile, combine the rice mix and beans in a glass bowl. Microwave for 3 minutes or until warmed through. Pour two-thirds of the dressing over the rice mixture and stir to combine.
Slice the chicken. Divide the rice mixture among bowls. Top with the chicken and pineapple. Drizzle with the remaining dressing and top with fresh coriander and chilli. Serve with lime wedges.

recipes.title: Lemongrass and chilli chicken
recipes.description: Want a weeknight meal that packs a punch? Try this lemongrass and chilli chicken dish!
ingredients: 1 long red chilli, seeded, finely chopped
20.00 ml lemongrass paste or finely chopped lemongrass
instructions: Use a large sharp knife to cut each chicken breast in half horizontally. Place in a large bowl. Add chilli, garlic, ginger, peanut oil, half the soy sauce and half the lemongrass. Toss to combine. Cover with plastic wrap. Place in the fridge for 10 mins to develop the flavours.
Meanwhile, place the rice wine vinegar, sugar, sesame oil, remaining soy sauce and remaining lemongrass in a small bowl. Stir to combine.
Heat a chargrill on medium. Cook the chicken for 3 mins each side or until cooked through. Transfer to a plate and cover with foil. Set aside for 5 mins to rest. Thickly slice.
Cook onion, bok choy and snow peas on the grill for 1-2 mins each side or until lightly charred. Transfer to a bowl. Drizzle with rice wine vinegar mixture and toss to combine.
Divide the bok choy mixture and rice evenly among serving plates. Top with chicken to serve.

recipes.title: Sweet potatoes with chicken and jalapeño slaw
recipes.description: They say 'eat the rainbow' and that could not be more true of this colourful sweet potato parcel. Packed with protein-rich black beans, this dish is hearty but low in fat.
ingredients: 1 long fresh green chilli, deseeded, finely chopped
40.00 ml chopped fresh coriander, plus extra leaves, to serve
10.60 gm fresh lime juice, plus lime wedges, to serve
4.60 gm olive oil, plus extra, to serve
instructions: Preheat oven to 200C/180C fan forced. Line a large baking tray with baking paper. Prick the sweet potatoes all over with a fork and place on the prepared tray.
Bake the sweet potatoes, turning halfway through cooking, for 50-55 minutes or until tender when pierced with a skewer. Set aside to cool slightly.
Meanwhile, combine the black beans, chicken, tomato, shallot, chilli, cottage cheese and half the coriander in a large bowl. Season.
Place the cabbage, jalapeño, remaining coriander, lime juice and olive oil in a bowl and toss to combine.

Make a long cut along the top of each potato. Gently separate the sides and use a fork to lightly mash the flesh. Divide the black bean filling among the sweet potatoes. Return to the oven and bake for 10 minutes or until heated through. Top with the jalapeño slaw and extra coriander. Drizzle with extra olive oil. Serve with lime.

recipes.title: 4-ingredient cheesy baked Mexican chicken
recipes.description: For a super-easy weeknight dinner, you can't beat this cheesy Mexican baked chicken – you only need 4 ingredients!
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180C/160C fan forced. Lightly grease a 1.5L (6 cup) baking dish.
Combine the black beans and half the pasta sauce in a bowl. Season to taste. Pour into the prepared dish. Sprinkle over 100g (1 cup) cheese. Place the chicken on top.
Spoon over the remaining sauce and scatter over the remaining 100g (1 cup) cheese. Bake for 30-35 minutes or until the cheese is golden and the chicken is cooked through.

recipes.title: Brown rice bowl with spiced chicken
recipes.description: Who doesn't love a tasty rice bowl! This one is packed with fresh salad, vegetable and tender spiced chicken! Save leftovers for a delicious lunch the next day!
ingredients: 500g butternut pumpkin, peeled, seeded, cut into 2cm pieces
instructions: Bring a large saucepan of boiling water to the boil over medium-high heat. Add rice and cook for 25 mins or until tender. Drain well.

Meanwhile, preheat oven to 200°C. Line a baking tray with baking paper. Combine the paprika, turmeric, cumin and ground coriander in a small bowl. Combine pumpkin and half the oil in a large bowl. Sprinkle with half the paprika mixture. Season. Toss to combine. Arrange pumpkin mixture in a single layer on the lined tray. Bake for 25 mins or until pumpkin is tender.

Combine the chicken and remaining paprika mixture and oil in a bowl. Heat a barbecue grill or chargrill on medium. Cook chicken for 3 mins each side or until cooked through. Transfer to a plate. Cover. Set aside for 5 mins to rest. Slice.
Place yoghurt, half the mint and half the coriander leaves in a blender. Blend until almost smooth. Season to taste.
Divide rice among serving bowls. Top with pumpkin, chicken, avocado and tomato. Drizzle with yoghurt dressing. Sprinkle with pepitas and remaining mint and coriander leaves.

recipes.title: Sesame chicken and quinoa salad
recipes.description: Change up boring work lunches with this sesame chicken and quinoa salad!
instructions: Place quinoa and 1 1/2 cups cold water in a medium saucepan over high heat. Cover. Bring to the boil. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 10 to 12 minutes or until liquid is absorbed and quinoa is tender. Set aside to cool.
Combine quinoa, chicken, cabbage, carrot, onion and sesame seeds in a bowl. Season with pepper. Toss to combine.
Whisk soy sauce, vinegar, oils and sugar in a jug until well combined and sugar is dissolved. Drizzle over chicken
Serve salad sprinkled with wasabi peas

recipes.title: White sourdough
recipes.description: Master the art of how to make sourdough bread with our step-by-step recipe. Learn how to create a starter, levain and the loaf itself with our expert tips.
ingredients: 250g strong white bread flour preferably organic or stoneground
100g strong white bread flour preferably organic or stoneground
1kg strong white bread flour preferably organic or stoneground, plus extra for dusting
instructions: Day 1: To begin your starter, mix 50g flour with 50g tepid water in a jar or, better still, a plastic container. Make sure all the flour is incorporated and leave, semi-uncovered, at room temperature for 24 hrs.
Day 2: Mix 50g flour with 50g tepid water and stir into yesterday’s mixture. Make sure all the flour is incorporated and leave, semi-uncovered, at room temperature for another 24 hrs.
Day 3: Mix 50g flour with 50g tepid water and stir into yesterday’s mixture. Make sure all the flour is incorporated and leave, semi-uncovered, at room temperature for another 24 hrs.

Day 4: You should start to see some activity in the mixture now; there should be some bubbles forming and bubbling on top. Mix 50g flour with 50g tepid water and stir into yesterday’s mixture. Make sure all the flour is incorporated and leave, semi-uncovered, at room temperature for another 24 hrs.
Day 5: The mixture should be very active now and ready for making your levain. If it’s not bubbling, continue to feed it on a daily basis until it does. When it’s ready, it should smell like yogurt.

You now have a starter, which is the base to the bread. You’ll need to look after it, but naming is optional! Keep it in the fridge (it will stay dormant) and 24 hrs before you want to use it, pour half of it off and feed it with 100g flour and 100g water. Leave it at room temperature and it should become active again. The longer the starter has been dormant, the more times it will need to be refreshed – the process of pouring off half the starter and replacing it with new flour and water – to reactivate. If your starter is ready to use, a teaspoonful of the mixture should float in warm water.

For the levain Mix 1 tbsp of the starter with 100g flour and 100g water (this is the same process as feeding the starter, but you should do this in a new, separate bowl, keeping the original starter as back-up, as this is the mixture you'll use to bake your bread). Leave the levain for 8 hrs at room temperature until it becomes active. When ready, a teaspoonful of the mixture should float in warm water.

For the bread Pour 600g tepid water into the levain and stir with a rubber spatula to mix together – don’t worry if there are unmixed bits of levain. Tip in the flour and mix everything together with a rubber spatula to make a rough dough, ensuring all the flour is incorporated evenly and that there are no dry bits up the side of the bowl. Cover and leave somewhere warm for at least 30 mins, or up to 4 hrs.

Sprinkle over the salt and add 50g water to the dough. Pinch and scrunch the salt and water through the dough with your hands. If the dough goes stringy (like old chewing gum), just keep working it until it’s one smooth texture. Leave for another 15 mins.

Wet your hands, grab the dough from one side and stretch it over itself, then repeat with the other side. This stretching technique helps develop the gluten. Pick the dough up and curl it around onto itself, then cover and leave for another 20-30 mins. Repeat this process two more times (three in total), then leave the dough for another 2-3 hrs until it’s risen by about 30% and looks bubbly and soft.

Using a rubber spatula, scrape the dough out onto a lightly floured work surface and split in two. Fold each piece onto itself to create a ball, then leave uncovered for 30 mins. The dough balls will spread during this time.

Dust two bread-proving baskets generously with flour. Scrape one of the balls of dough off the work surface, then fold it onto itself to create a tight ball that’s trapped in all the air. Lift the ball into a basket, seam-side up, then transfer to the fridge to chill overnight, or for up to 18 hrs. Repeat with the other dough ball.

Heat the oven to 240C/220C fan/gas 9 and put a lidded casserole dish in the oven to heat. Cut a sheet of baking parchment into a square slightly larger than the base of one of the loaves. Carefully remove the hot casserole dish from the oven and remove the lid. Invert one loaf onto the baking parchment, then, working quickly, score the top at an angle. Use the corners of the parchment to lift the loaf into the casserole dish. Cover with the lid and bake for 30 mins, then carefully uncover and continue to bake for another 10 mins (or longer for a darker finish). Carefully lift the bread out of the dish using a spatula, transfer to a wire rack and leave to cool to room temperature before slicing. Repeat with the second loaf.

recipes.title: Focaccia
recipes.description: Make a simple, homemade version of this classic Italian bread. Serve our rosemary focaccia alongside pasta dishes or enjoy with green salads
ingredients: 500g strong bread flour plus extra for dusting
5 tbsp olive oil plus extra for the tin and to serve
¼ small bunch of rosemary sprigs picked
instructions: Tip the flour into a large mixing bowl. Mix the yeast into one side of the flour, and the fine salt into the other side.
Then mix everything together, this initial seperation prevents the salt from killing the yeast.
Make a well in the middle of the flour and add 2 tbsp oil and 350-400ml lukewarm water, adding it gradually until you have a slightly sticky dough (you may not need all the water).

Sprinkle the work surface with flour and tip the dough onto it, scraping around the sides of the bowl. Knead for 5-10 mins until your dough is soft and less sticky. Put the dough into a clean bowl, cover with a tea towel and leave to prove for 1 hr until doubled in size.
Oil a rectangle, shallow tin (25 x 35cm). Tip the dough onto the work surface, then stretch it to fill the tin. Cover with a tea towel and leave to prove for another 35-45 mins.
Heat the oven to 220C/200C fan/gas 7. Press your fingers into the dough to make dimples.
Mix together 1½ tbsp olive oil, 1 tbsp water and the flaky salt and drizzle over the bread. Push sprigs of rosemary into the dimples in the dough.
Bake for 20 mins until golden. Whilst the bread is still hot, drizzle over 1-2 tbsp olive oil. Cut into squares and serve warm or cold with extra olive oil, if you like.

recipes.title: Chicken pasta bake
recipes.description: Enjoy this gooey cheese and chicken pasta bake for the ultimate weekday family dinner. Serve straight from the dish with a dressed green salad
ingredients: 4 skinless chicken breasts, sliced into strips
½ small bunch of parsley finely chopped
instructions: Heat 2 tbsp of the oil in a pan over a medium heat and fry the onion gently for 10-12 mins. Add the garlic and chilli flakes and cook for 1 min. Tip in the tomatoes and sugar and season to taste. Simmer uncovered for 20 mins or until thickened, then stir through the mascarpone.
Heat 1 tbsp of oil in a non-stick frying pan. Season the chicken and fry for 5-7 mins or until the chicken is cooked through.

Heat the oven to 220C/200C fan/gas 7. Cook the penne following pack instructions. Drain and toss with the remaining oil. Tip the pasta into a medium sized ovenproof dish. Stir in the chicken and pour over the sauce. Top with the cheddar, mozzarella and parsley. Bake for 20 mins or until golden brown and bubbling.

recipes.title: Easy chicken curry
recipes.description: This easy staple chicken curry is a fantastic recipe for family dinners. It's made with just a handful of ingredients and is enriched with creamy yogurt
ingredients: 3 tbsp medium spice paste (tikka works well)
1 small bunch of coriander leaves chopped
naan breads or cooked basmati rice, to serve
instructions: Heat the oil in a flameproof casserole dish or large frying pan over a medium heat. Add the onion and a generous pinch of salt and fry for 8-10 mins, or until the onion has turned golden brown and sticky. Add the garlic and ginger, cooking for a further minute.

Chop the chicken into chunky 3cm pieces, add to the pan and fry for 5 mins before stirring through the spice paste and tomatoes, along with 250ml water. Bring to the boil, lower to a simmer and cook on a gentle heat uncovered for 25-30 mins or until rich and slightly reduced. Stir though the yogurt, coriander and ground almonds, season and serve with warm naan or fluffy basmati rice.

recipes.title: Sausage ragu
recipes.description: Feed the family this comforting, budget-friendly sausage ragu with pasta. You can freeze the leftovers for another time and it tastes just as good
ingredients: grated parmesan and ½ small bunch parsley, leaves roughly chopped, to serve
instructions: Heat 2 tbsp of the oil in a saucepan over a medium heat. Fry the onion with a pinch of salt for 7 mins. Add the garlic, chilli and rosemary, and cook for 1 min more. Tip in the tomatoes and sugar, and simmer for 20 mins.

Heat the remaining oil in a medium frying pan over a medium heat. Squeeze the sausagemeat from the skins and fry, breaking it up with a wooden spoon, for 5-7 mins until golden. Add to the sauce with the milk and lemon zest, then simmer for a further 5 mins. To freeze, leave to cool completely and transfer to large freezerproof bags.
Cook the pasta following pack instructions. Drain and toss with the sauce. Scatter over the parmesan and parsley leaves to serve.

recipes.title: Creamy pesto & kale pasta
recipes.description: Enjoy our creamy pesto and kale pasta as a tasty and nutritious supper. Make it with just a handful of ingredients and storecupboard staples
ingredients: 300g wholemeal  pasta (penne or mafalda work well)
4 tbsp fresh or jar pesto or vegetarian alternative
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pan over a medium heat. Fry the onions for 10 mins until softened and beginning to caramelise. Add the kale and 100ml water, then cover and cook for 5 mins more, or until the kale has wilted.

Cook the pasta following pack instructions. Drain, reserving a little of the cooking water. Toss the pasta with the onion mixture, soft cheese and pesto, adding a splash of the reserved cooking water to loosen, if needed. Season.

recipes.title: Fish pie mac ’n’ cheese
recipes.description: Combine fish pie with mac 'n' cheese to make this crowd-pleasing dinner. The dish freezes well, so you can make ahead if you like for busy weeknights
ingredients: 300g fish pie mix (smoked fish, white fish and salmon)
instructions: Pour the milk into a large pan and add the flour and butter. Set over a medium heat and whisk continuously until you have a smooth, thick white sauce. Remove from the heat, add the mustard, most of the cheese (save a handful for the top), peas and parsley.
Meanwhile, boil the pasta in a large pan of water following pack instructions until just cooked. Drain.

Heat the oven to 200C/180C fan/gas 6. Tip the pasta into the sauce and add half the fish, stir everything together then tip into a large baking dish. Top with the rest of the fish, pushing it into the pasta a little, then scatter with the remaining cheese. Bake for 30 mins until golden, then serve with salad, if you like. Can be chilled and eaten within three days or frozen for up to a month. Defrost in the fridge, then reheat in a microwave or oven until piping hot.

recipes.title: Speedy lentil coconut curry
recipes.description: This quick and easy curry has such great depth of flavour – it tastes like it’s been cooked for hours. It's healthy too, as well as being low in fat and calories
ingredients: 1 red or green chilli roughly chopped
10g piece of ginger peeled and chopped
1 ½ tbsp tikka masala curry paste
4 tbsp light coconut or natural yogurt to serve
instructions: Put the onion, garlic, chilli, carrot and ginger in a food processor and blitz to a smooth paste.

Heat the oil in a medium saucepan over a medium heat and cook the veg paste for 4-5 mins until fragrant and starting to soften. Add the curry paste and cook for 1 min more, then add the lentils and stir to combine.
Pour in the coconut milk and 50-75ml water, and bring to the boil. Reduce the heat to a simmer and cook for 10 mins until thickened and creamy. Add the peas in the final 5 mins, and season well.
Stir in most of the coriander, then divide the curry between four bowls along with the rice. Sprinkle over the remaining coriander and top with the yogurt to serve.

recipes.title: Fajita-style pasta
recipes.description: Take the aromatic flavours of a classic Mexican fajita and combine with pasta for this easy, vibrant meal. It's an ideal Friday night dinner
ingredients: 2 large skinless chicken breasts cut into strips
1⁄2 small bunch of flat-leaf parsley finely chopped
grated parmesan or cheddar, to serve
instructions: Heat the oil in a large shallow casserole or frying pan. Add the chicken and fry for 5 mins over a medium heat until golden all over. Remove and set aside on a plate.

Put the onion and peppers in the same pan and fry over a medium heat for 8-10 mins. Add the garlic, dried herbs and spices and cook for 1 min. Add the tomato purée and cook for 2 mins. Return the chicken to the pan and pour in the cream, stirring to combine. Season to taste.

Cook the pasta following pack instructions, then drain and reserve 150ml of the cooking water. Add the pasta to the pan with 50ml of the water and stir everything together over the heat. Add a little more water to loosen if needed. Season to taste and stir through the parsley. Divide between six bowls and top with a little cheese and extra chopped parsley, if you like. This can be packed into a lunchbox and eaten cold, too.

recipes.title: The best spaghetti bolognese recipe
recipes.description: Our best ever spaghetti bolognese is super easy and a true Italian classic with a meaty, chilli sauce. This pasta bolognese recipe is sure to become a family favourite.
ingredients: 4 rashers smoked streaky bacon finely chopped
2-3 sprigs rosemary leaves picked and finely chopped
small pack basil leaves picked, ¾ finely chopped and the rest left whole for garnish
1 red chilli deseeded and finely chopped (optional)
75g parmesan grated, plus extra to serve
instructions: Put a large saucepan on a medium heat and add 1 tbsp olive oil.
Add 4 finely chopped bacon rashers and fry for 10 mins until golden and crisp.

Reduce the heat and add the 2 onions, 2 carrots, 2 celery sticks, 2 garlic cloves and the leaves from 2-3 sprigs rosemary, all finely chopped, then fry for 10 mins. Stir the veg often until it softens.
Increase the heat to medium-high, add 500g beef mince and cook stirring for 3-4 mins until the meat is browned all over.

Add 2 tins plum tomatoes, the finely chopped leaves from ¾ small pack basil, 1 tsp dried oregano, 2 bay leaves, 2 tbsp tomato purée, 1 beef stock, 1 deseeded and finely chopped red chilli (if using), 125ml red wine and 6 halved cherry tomatoes. Stir with a wooden spoon, breaking up the plum tomatoes.
Bring to the boil, reduce to a gentle simmer and cover with a lid. Cook for 1 hr 15 mins stirring occasionally, until you have a rich, thick sauce.
Add the 75g grated parmesan, check the seasoning and stir.
When the bolognese is nearly finished, cook 400g spaghetti following the pack instructions.
Drain the spaghetti and either stir into the bolognese sauce, or serve the sauce on top. Serve with more grated parmesan, the remaining basil leaves and crusty bread, if you like.

recipes.title: Creamy garlic pasta
recipes.description: This creamy tagliatelle recipe makes a comforting midweek meal. Any long pasta will work, so use whatever you have in the cupboard
instructions: Begin by cooking the pasta following pack instructions. Meanwhile, melt the butter in your largest frying pan. Once foaming, add the garlic and 25 twists of a black pepper mill. Cook for 4-5 mins, until the garlic is light golden and fragrant.

Stir in the flour to form a paste. Stir for 1-2 mins, then slowly whisk in the chicken stock until you have a smooth sauce. Pour in the double cream and sprinkle in most of the parmesan. Stir until everything is melted and combined, then season to taste.
Transfer the pasta straight into the sauce, alongside a good splash of the cooking water. Mix thoroughly, adding a little more pasta water if necessary, until you have a thick and glossy sauce.
Divide between four bowls and serve topped with the chopped parsley and remaining parmesan.

recipes.title: Meatball black bean chilli
recipes.description: Double the amounts for this one-pot black bean chilli, then freeze the leftovers for busy days. It tastes just as great reheated as it does freshly cooked
ingredients: ½ large bunch coriander leaves and stalks chopped
1 heaped tbsp light brown soft sugar
2 x 400g cans black beans drained and rinsed
instructions: Heat the oil in a large flameproof casserole dish over a medium heat. Fry the meatballs for 5 mins until browned, then transfer to a plate with a slotted spoon.

Fry the onion and peppers with a pinch of salt for 7 mins. Add the coriander stalks, garlic, paprika and cumin and fry for 1 min more. Tip in the sugar, tomatoes and beans, and bring to a simmer. Season, return the meatballs to the pan and cook, covered, for 15 mins. To freeze, leave to cool completely and transfer to large freezerproof bags.
Serve the chilli with the rice and the coriander leaves scattered over.

recipes.title: Creamy salmon, leek & potato traybake
recipes.description: Nestle leeks, potato and capers around salmon fillets to make this easy traybake for two. It's great as an midweek meal, or for a more romantic occasion
ingredients: 1 tbsp capers plus extra to serve
1 tbsp chives plus extra to serve
instructions: Heat the oven to 200C/180C fan/gas 6. Bring a medium pan of water to the boil. Add the potatoes and cook for 8 mins. Drain and leave to steam-dry in a colander for a few minutes. Toss the potatoes with ½ of the oil and plenty of seasoning in a baking tray. Put in the oven for 20 mins, tossing halfway through the cooking time.

Meanwhile, heat the remaining oil in a frying pan over a medium heat. Add the leek and fry for 5 mins, or until beginning to soften. Stir through the garlic for 1 min, then add the cream, capers and 75ml hot water, then bring to the boil. Stir through the chives.

Heat the grill to high. Pour the creamy leek mixture over the potatoes, then sit the salmon fillets on top. Grill for 7-8 mins, or until just cooked through. Serve topped with extra chives and capers and a salad on the side, if you like.

recipes.title: Spicy chickpea stew
recipes.description: Make a filling meal that encourages healthy gut bacteria with this chickpea and cauliflower stew. A valuable plant-based protein, chickpeas are full of fibre
ingredients: 2 green peppers deseeded and cut into cubes
½ lemon juiced, flesh scooped out and white pith removed, then zest finely chopped (you’ll need 2 tsp)
instructions: Heat the oil in a large lidded pan over a medium heat and fry the onions for 10 mins, stirring often until golden. Stir in the peppers and cook for 5 mins more.
Add the chilli powder, coriander and cumin, stir briefly, then tip in the passata and chickpeas along with the liquid from the cans.
Stir in the bouillon powder, raisins and lemon zest, then add the cauliflower. Cover tightly and simmer over a medium heat for 15-20 mins until the cauliflower is tender. Stir in half the parsley.

Meanwhile, put the couscous in a heatproof bowl and pour over 175ml boiling water from the kettle. Stir in the lemon juice, then cover and let stand for about 10 mins until the couscous has absorbed the liquid and is tender. Stir in the toasted flaked almonds and most of the remaining parsley.

Divide half the couscous between two plates and top with half the chickpea stew and the rest of the parsley. Leave the remainder to cool for another day. Will keep covered and chilled for up to three days. Reheat the stew in a pan over a low heat with a splash of water until piping hot. Reheat the couscous in the microwave.

recipes.title: Veggie sausage casserole
recipes.description: Make this casserole with veggie sausages and butterbeans for a flavourful family meal that delivers four of your 5-a-day. Serve with warm crusty bread
ingredients: few sprigs of  thyme rosemary or sage
instructions: Heat the oil in a large flameproof casserole dish over a medium-high heat. Once shimmering, add the sausages and quickly stir to coat in the oil. Cook for 5-7 mins until browned all over, then scoop out and set aside on a plate. Turn the heat down to medium and stir in the onion, celery and carrot with a big pinch of salt. Cook for 8-10 mins until softened but not coloured.

Stir in the garlic, paprika and fennel seeds, if using, and cook for another 1-2 mins until fragrant. Stir in the herb sprigs and the tomato purée. Stir well to coat everything and cook for 5 mins until the tomato purée has caramelised and turned dark red. Add the vinegar, tomatoes, stock and beans, along with their liquid, then rinse out the tomato can with water and add that too. Bring to a simmer and return the sausages to the pan. Simmer gently for 40-45 mins, stirring frequently, until the sauce has thickened. Season to taste, remove the herb sprigs and discard.
Drizzle over the pesto and serve with warm crusty bread, if you like.

recipes.title: Chicken, leek & brown rice stir-fry
recipes.description: Combine the classic flavours of chicken and chorizo with kale and rice for a substantial yet speedy dinner, taking less than 20 minutes to make
ingredients: 1 leek halved lengthways and finely sliced
80g kale any tough stalks removed, leaves roughly chopped
instructions: Heat the oil in a frying pan over a high heat and fry the chicken for 3 mins. Stir in the chorizo and cook for 2 mins more until the chicken is light golden and the chorizo has released its fat. Scoop the chicken and chorizo into a bowl using a slotted spoon, leaving as much oil in the pan as you can. Set aside.
Tip the leek and red pepper into the pan and cook for 2 mins, stirring frequently until slightly softened. Add the kale and fry for 1 min more until the leaves have just started to wilt at the edges.

Drizzle in the soy sauce and vinegar and scatter in the rice, breaking up any large chunks with a wooden spoon. Stir the chicken and chorizo back into the pan and toss everything together to combine. Cook for 3 mins until the rice is heated through, then serve.

recipes.title: Gnocchi cacio e pepe
recipes.description: Enjoy a comforting bowl of gnocchi with parmesan and black pepper. It's simple but utterly delicious – and the best part is, it only takes seven minutes to make
ingredients: 60g parmesan or vegetarian alternative, finely grated
instructions: Cook the gnocchi in a large pan of lightly salted, boiling water. Drain and reserve 200ml of the cooking water.

Heat the butter in a large frying pan. Add the gnocchi, cheese and pepper as well as 150ml of the cooking water, raise the heat a little and stir vigorously until melted and the gnocchi is well coated. Pour in more of the reserved water if you like it saucier. Season with a little salt. Transfer the gnocchi to bowls and serve with a mixed salad, if you like.

recipes.title: Roasted carrot & whipped feta tart
recipes.description: Make the most of budget-friendly carrots with this colourful veggie tart, topped with lemon rind curls and homemade carrot-top pesto
